chapter: Sidemen, mixed bands, the Apollo and Lena Horne
title: The cooperative orchestra with Red Norvo and the Bar Harbor story
summary: He and Red Norvo traded fronting a shared band when each had work; Barnet denies he was fired in Bar Harbor, saying it was Norvo's trip.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Yeah, well what, Red Norvo, right?

Well, Red and I, you know, actually had an orchestra together. When neither one of us could get steady work. When he got the job he'd stand in front of the band, and usually that was when Mildred Bailey would work, he'd -- and he'd do his bit with the xylophone, and I would sit down and play saxophone in the section. And when it was my job, Red would play piano. But it was the same band.

Oh, there was -- let's see, there was a trombone player by the name of Russ Jenner. Eddie Sauter. Chris Griffin. Oh, a wonderful trumpet player who later made some records with Red. Oh, I can't think of his name. Bob White was a drummer. It was a five brass, four saxophone band. I can't really recall. It gets a little blurred there

because I can't even tell you who else was in the saxophone section, except I think -- I'm not sure, but I think that Hymie Schertzer was in that band. I could be wrong, but I seem to remember him. Because that was a -- it was a very loose relationship. In other words, jobs weren't that often. We'd play something with Mildred, and then maybe I'd get a few one nighters and we'd load in the automobiles and take off and play them and come back. And sometimes the guys that played, like Mildred's jobs were maybe in a theater in Newark or something, the guys that played that wouldn't go play the one nighters, so we had to substitute. But contrary to what Eddie Sauter says, one thing he says is that I took the band up to Bar Harbor, Maine and got fired for playing undanceable music. It wasn't me. It was Red Norvo that took the band up there, and I wasn't even in the band. In one of the books this is a quotation. Because I have never been in Bar Harbor in my life, so I couldn't have -- that's one atrocity that I wasn't responsible for.
